children.objective: In src/candidate.cu, isolate the CTA-local reduction: replace reduce0's modulo-based shared-memory tree with a warp-centric or permitted CUB block reduction, while keeping the 128-thread launch geometry, one input per lane, multi-stage scratch schedule, and final copy fixed. The existing warpReduceSum helper is not currently used by reduce0, so it is a natural comparison point, not a measured improvement. Handle tails safely and preserve exact signed sums. Validate all checks and compare complete-run timings; report whether the local change helps independently of launch topology.
children.subject: Isolate and improve the CTA-local reduction

children.objective: In src/candidate.cu, focus the experiment on the large-n global schedule: the supplied n=4194304 path currently launches reduction stages producing 32768, 256, 2, then 1 partials, followed by a copy. Explore work partitioning and partial counts that reduce stages and/or write the final result directly to out, retaining enough first-stage parallelism. Keep the small-n path to T3's scope. Alternative CTA implementations are allowed, but where practical compare against the existing CTA reduction so stage-count gains are distinguishable from T1's block-reduction gains. Never rely on uninitialized scratch or implicit inter-block ordering. Validate the complete supported domain and compare total-run timings.
children.subject: Reduce large-n global stages and partial-sum traffic

children.objective: In src/candidate.cu, focus on supported small n: compare a one-CTA reduction that writes directly to out against the existing staged reduction plus copy, and choose any crossover from generic measured sizes rather than exact test values. The n=1 baseline already performs only a device copy, so use it as a control instead of assuming a kernel launch is faster. Keep the large-n path to T2's scope; validate all checks and compare complete-run timings.
children.subject: Measure a direct small-n path and crossover
